title: Minor-piece endings

D0.outcome: Explains that bishop against knight depends on the pawn structure: the bishop is better with pawns on both wings, the knight is at least equal in locked one-wing structures.

D1.outcome: Predicts which side stands better in minor-piece endings that differ by one feature (pawns on both wings, a passed pawn, locked structure).

D2.outcome: In unlabeled endings, picks the plan (king to the centre, create a passed pawn on the other wing) and the evaluation band, and separates same-coloured and opposite-coloured bishop endings.

D3.outcome: States the tendencies and their exceptions for opposite-coloured bishops (usually drawn, but two distant passers or pawns on both wings can win).

conditions: Pawns on both wings favour the bishop, more so with unbalanced wings and passed pawns.
Same-coloured bishops: an extra pawn usually wins by exchanging into a won pawn ending.
contrasts: A locked one-wing structure where the knight is at least equal.
Opposite-coloured bishops 'always draw' (two connected passers win; Capablanca wins G9 anyway).
Swapping far-flank pawns that does not change the structure.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.PASSED.D2: the passed pawn decides most minor-piece endings
